justification: B (solution-D) shows every failure cause and its status inline at the branch (e.g. Results.Problem("payment-declined", statusCode: 402)) and accumulates validation codes in explicit rule-ordered statements, while A (solution-C) routes the same semantics through library combinators (Zip/Traverse/Ensure/ToHttpResult) whose accumulation order, status mapping, and even GET /products' 200 path are only visible in the library, not the file. A's typed closed error hierarchies and rules-vs-HTTP separation are genuine strengths, but its POST happy path is fragmented across callbacks, rule order lives in Zip argument order, and its single null-forgiving pricing assumption is matched by B's one `!` wart — so as the owning maintainer I prefer B's zero-vocabulary, at-a-glance branches.
